cv-polar-title: FLAT · POLAR (AE disk) · ruler = straight chord
cv-cart-title: FLAT · CARTESIAN (lat/lon as x‑y grid) · ruler = straight line
cap-polar: Polar map (the flat‑earth disk). The same endpoints plotted at r = 90°−φ, θ = λ, joined by straight ruler lines — how anyone measures a flat map. Each southern segment comes out far longer than its identical northern mirror, and the two pairs are distorted by different amounts.
cap-cart: Cartesian map. The same endpoints read as x = λ, y = φ, joined by straight ruler lines. Mirror pairs stay equal to each other — the grid is symmetric across the equator — but every length is inflated relative to the great‑circle distance, and by a different factor for each segment.

exp3-verdict: Verdict rule: if the two mirror legs measure the same, the globe survives. If the southern one is really {ratio2}× the northern one, the disc survives. Airlines settle this daily: Sydney–Santiago is about 11,400 km and is flown non-stop in roughly 12½ hours, which no aircraft could do if it were the ~25,000 km the disc requires.
